tickets.title: P2-115: /api/health's feedConnected is Account.All.Count > 0 and can never be false
tickets.defect:
`addons/McpBridgeAddOn.cs`, the `/api/health` case (around line 443):

```csharp
accountCount = Account.All != null ? Account.All.Count : 0;
connectedToFeed = accountCount > 0;
...
return new { status = "ok", ..., accounts = accountCount, feedConnected = connectedToFeed };
```

**The field has exactly one reachable value.** A running NT8 always reports at least its Simulator accounts, so `feedConnected` is `true` on every call, on every box, forever. It is not a weak measurement of the data feed; it is not a measurement of the data feed. It is a constant wearing the name of the one thing a caller checks before trusting a price. `accounts` is already reported honestly one line above, so today the payload carries the same number twice with one of them mislabelled.

MEASURED LIVE, 2026-08-15, and this is the whole consequence argument:

  * 14:20 UTC, NT8 on a DORMANT `Playback` connection with no replay running and no tradeable market at all: `feedConnected: true`, while `nt_quote MNQ 09-26` returned a price frozen eight days at `2026-08-07T01:45` with `volume: 0`, `ES 09-26` had never been subscribed, and three ATM orders placed on Sim101 sat at `OrderState.Initialized` and were never routed anywhere.
  * 14:54 UTC, real broker attached: `feedConnected: true`, `MNQ` a live book at `30151.75 / 30155` on 1,925,425 volume.

**It did not change value when the thing it names changed completely.** It also misled the agent investigating it, in writing, within five minutes -- which is exactly when a status field does its damage: it is consulted at the moment someone is about to trust something else.
tickets.spec:
TWO changes.

1. NEW FILE `addons/BridgeFeedStatus.cs`, namespace `NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.AddOns`, holding ALL the logic:

```csharp
public static class BridgeFeedStatus
{
    public static bool IsMarketDataConnected(string[] names, string[] providers, string[] statuses)
}
```

   Rules, all pinned by the tests:
   * TRUE only if at least one entry is BOTH connected AND non-simulated.
   * "Connected" is an exact, case-insensitive match on the string `Connected`. Anything else -- `Disconnected`, `Connecting`, `ConnectionLost`, null, empty, whitespace, an unrecognised word -- is NOT connected.
   * "Simulated" is an exact, case-insensitive match on `Simulator` or `Playback`. Those two and only those two. Null or unrecognised provider is NOT positively identified as real, so it does not count toward TRUE either.
   * Null arrays, empty arrays, and arrays of differing length must not throw. Iterate to the SHORTEST length and return false rather than indexing past the end.
   * Return `false` for no connections at all.

   The three parallel string arrays are deliberate and are not to be replaced by an NT8 type: this class must name NO NinjaTrader type, or it lands in the set nothing can execute. See context.

2. `addons/McpBridgeAddOn.cs`, the `/api/health` case: build the three arrays from `Account.All` -- `a.Name`, `a.Provider.ToString()`, `a.Connection == null ? null : a.Connection.Status.ToString()` -- inside the existing try/catch, and set `connectedToFeed` from `BridgeFeedStatus.IsMarketDataConnected(...)`. Delete `connectedToFeed = accountCount > 0;`. `accounts = accountCount` stays exactly as it is; it was always honest.

Leave a comment at BOTH sites recording that the old expression could not be false, and that it was measured reading `true` against a dormant Playback connection with no market. Reference P2-115.

DO NOT: touch any *Tests.cs file, the csproj, or anything under vendor/; add a new field to the health payload (the `connections` detail view is a separate, deliberate decision -- see context); rename `feedConnected`; put ANY of the classification logic in McpBridgeAddOn.cs; add a config switch; or use `Contains`/`StartsWith` for either match.
tickets.context:
WHY EXACT MATCHES AND NOT `Contains`. `P2-38` on this codebase was `Name.StartsWith("Sim")` -- a user-chosen string read as a fact about money, which let an account called "SimpsonFund" through a safety gate. `Provider` and `ConnectionStatus` are platform enums, so an exact match on their `ToString()` is a different and legitimate act, but it must stay exact. A substring test here would make a provider named `PlaybackBrokerX` invisible.

WHY FAIL CLOSED ON UNKNOWNS. This field's failure mode is a caller trusting a stale price. An unrecognised status must not read as a working feed. Null, blank and anything not positively identified as connected all answer false -- and there is a test for the null case.

WHY THE THREE STRING ARRAYS. `addons/McpBridgeAddOn.cs` is in NO test build -- it names NinjaTrader types the harness cannot resolve, which is `P2-27` and is still open. Every class in this repo that is actually executed by a test (`BridgeAccountResolver`, `BridgeFlattenPlan`, `BridgeClosePlan`, `BridgeAccountScope`, `BridgeOrderQuery`, `BridgeLockoutGate`) names no NT8 type for exactly that reason. Taking an `Account[]` here would move this logic straight back into the untestable set, and the ticket would ship with a source gate's worth of evidence instead of six executed assertions.

WHY NOT ALSO ADD A `connections` LIST, which is the obvious improvement. Deliberately out of scope. The tests pin one boolean; adding a payload field is a contract change for every existing client of /api/health and belongs with a decision about the MCP wrapper's schema. The plan entry records it as the follow-up. Resist it here.

A NOTE ON THE REST OF THE PAYLOAD, so you do not 'fix' it: `status = "ok"` is also a constant, but defensibly so -- an unreachable endpoint returns no payload at all, so that constant carries its meaning in being RECEIVED. And `guarding` is character-for-character the same expression as `isArmed` on /api/riskguard/version, which is one fact under two names. Both are recorded in the plan entry and neither is this ticket.
